title: Production-used .abfs has unclosed generation provenance and a filename that omits a real channel (g)
symptom: For the historical 2D W asset W_6s3p3d2f1g_1e-6.abfs (SHA256 bfa1a46ace6624387fcb5a225199f965b85e3688970902d86a2ceffd8c983f52) the production combination with a scalar GTH PP and a specific physical W NAO is proven, but the PP/NAO/parameters used to GENERATE it cannot be established. The same historical directory holds a fully-relativistic ONCV W.upf and a GTH-SOC PP, and the historical W NAO filename omits the 'g' although the content has it.
root_cause: Co-located files are not generation provenance: no generation STRU/INPUT, run log or generation manifest exists, so the ABFS generator PP/NAO/parameters stay open. The NAO filename is also an unreliable label for the real channel composition (the header lists g, the filename does not).
minimal_fix: Import such assets with an explicit two-part tag ('production combination verified / generation provenance unclosed'), keep the original file byte-identical at its recorded hash, and read channel counts from the file header rather than the filename. Never label the file as generated by the matched scalar GTH PP/NAO.
validation: Re-check SHA256 bfa1a46ace6624387fcb5a225199f965b85e3688970902d86a2ceffd8c983f52, confirm the historical W NAO hash equals the production file hash, and verify from the header that the channel list contains g while the filename does not.
avoid: Do not infer the ABFS generation PP from other PP files in the same directory, and do not rewrite or rename the asset to 'fix' the filename - the original file must be preserved.

parameters.identity_rule: hash + file header, never filename suffix
